_about: Datasheet-derived PMBus register + decode map for the RED DSMC2 UCD power sequencers. Shared by ucd_dump (what to read) and ucd_decode (how to interpret). Command codes cited from TI UCD9090 (SLVSAG6)/UCD90160 (SLVSA95) datasheets and the TI PMBus 1.1/1.2 command reference. UCD9081 (SLUS753) is a DIFFERENT, non-PMBus part kept here only for completeness; on this hardware the live parts are UCD9090 (IOB/ISP) and UCD90160 (sensor) per the FW driver dispatch.

UCD9090.discriminator: ucd9090_set_page accepts page < 0x0B; MFR_MODEL (0x9A) ASCII = 'UCD9090'. Live confirm: IC_DEVICE_ID (0xFC) block read.

UCD90160.discriminator: ucd90160_set_page accepts page < 0x11; MFR_MODEL (0x9A) ASCII = 'UCD90160'. 16 valid pages vs 9090's 11 is the definitive offline discriminator.

UCD9081.note: NOT PMBus. 8-rail sequencer with a flat 0x00.. register file (RAILxx_* at fixed offsets), not PAGE-based. Different reg map entirely. Present as driver variant id 0 but NOT selected for IOB/ISP/sensor on this build, so not dumped by the paged path. Listed for completeness only.

_boards_about: board -> which UCD part + bus/addr. bus = shell logical I2C index. addr = 7-bit. Confirmed: COMPARISON.md (IOB 131-0725 + ISP 131-0724 both UCD9090); FW dispatch DAT_81407368={1,1,2}; live scan bus2.

iob.source: COMPARISON.md IOB 131-0725 UCD9090; scan bus2 0x70; E49 logs ucd9090_reg_write @0x70

isp.note: ISP board 131-0724 is also UCD9090 (COMPARISON.md). On a single-head body the ISP/IOB UCD may share bus2 0x70 (IOB carries it) OR the ISP board has its own 0x70 on its own bus head - confirm live with `read ucd isp` + a scan of each bus. Dual-ISP bodies have two.

sensor.source: FW dispatch variant 2 = ucd90160; E49_REFLOW_BENCH_LOG read i2c 2 0x65 (sensor side)

lcd7.note: Labeled 'LCD7 Power Monitor' in this session's scan. Determine part live via MFR_MODEL(0x9A)/IC_DEVICE_ID(0xFC). Likely a smaller monitor (UCD9081-class or a non-UCD INA/monitor); not in the power_seq dispatch, so no FW driver variant -> treat generically, read identity first.

rsb.note: `read ucd rsb` is accepted by the shell. Enumerate its bus/addr with per-bus scans; memory red-board-level says RSB is GPIO-only with no FW binary, so its 'UCD' may be a monitor only.

vout_mode.note: VOUT_MODE. Low 5 bits = signed 2's-complement exponent N (mode bits [7:5]=000 => LINEAR mode). VOUT (READ_VOUT 0x8B, VOUT_COMMAND 0x21, all VOUT limits) are LINEAR16: unsigned 16-bit mantissa V, value = V * 2^N. On UCD9090/90160 N is typically -12 (0x14 in the 5-bit field) => 1 LSB = 2^-12 V ~= 244 uV.

linear11.note: LINEAR11 (used by READ_VIN 0x88, READ_IOUT 0x8C, READ_TEMPERATURE 0x8D, all _LIMIT regs that are not VOUT, TON/TOFF are unsigned ms not LINEAR11). 16-bit word: top 5 bits = signed exponent E, low 11 bits = signed mantissa Y. value = Y * 2^E.
linear11.decode: Y = sign_extend_11bit(word & 0x7FF); E = sign_extend_5bit(word >> 11); value = Y * 2^E

registers.name: PAGE
registers.about: Selects the rail/page for all paged reads. WRITE this first (write i2c BUS ADDR 0x00 1 N) before reading paged regs. 0xFF = all pages.

registers.name: OPERATION
registers.about: On/off/margin control for the selected rail. 0x80=on, 0x00=off; margin bits [3:2]. (This is the reg FUN_8069446c writes to enable a rail.)

registers.name: ON_OFF_CONFIG
registers.about: How the rail turns on (CONTROL pin vs OPERATION cmd).

registers.name: VOUT_MODE
registers.about: Exponent for LINEAR16 VOUT on this page. Read once per page to decode all VOUT values.

registers.name: VOUT_COMMAND
registers.about: Nominal/target output voltage for the rail.

registers.name: VOUT_MARGIN_HIGH
registers.about: Margined-high test voltage.

registers.name: VOUT_MARGIN_LOW
registers.about: Margined-low test voltage.

registers.name: VOUT_OV_FAULT_LIMIT
registers.about: Over-voltage FAULT threshold. Rail shuts/faults above this.

registers.name: VOUT_OV_WARN_LIMIT
registers.about: Over-voltage WARN threshold.

registers.name: VOUT_UV_WARN_LIMIT
registers.about: Under-voltage WARN threshold.

registers.name: VOUT_UV_FAULT_LIMIT
registers.about: Under-voltage FAULT threshold. Rail faults below this - the usual power-seq boot killer.

registers.name: IOUT_OC_FAULT_LIMIT
registers.about: Over-current fault limit (if the rail has current sense).

registers.name: IOUT_OC_WARN_LIMIT
registers.about: Over-current warn limit.

registers.name: OT_FAULT_LIMIT
registers.about: Over-temperature fault limit.

registers.name: POWER_GOOD_ON
registers.about: Voltage at/above which this rail is declared power-good.

registers.name: POWER_GOOD_OFF
registers.about: Voltage at/below which power-good deasserts.

registers.name: TON_DELAY
registers.about: Turn-ON delay (ms) after this rail is commanded on = the SEQUENCING order knob. Lower = earlier in the sequence.

registers.name: TON_RISE
registers.about: Ramp time from 0 to regulation (ms).

registers.name: TON_MAX_FAULT_LIMIT
registers.about: Max time to reach power-good or fault (ms). A rail that never comes up trips this.

registers.name: TOFF_DELAY
registers.about: Turn-OFF delay (ms) = power-down sequence order.

registers.name: STATUS_BYTE
registers.about: Abbreviated per-rail status.

registers.name: STATUS_WORD
registers.about: Summary of all fault groups for the selected rail. Non-zero = something is wrong on this rail.

registers.name: STATUS_VOUT
registers.about: Per-rail OV/UV fault+warn bits. THE key reg for 'which rail dropped'. bit7=OV_FAULT bit6=OV_WARN bit5=UV_WARN bit4=UV_FAULT.

registers.name: STATUS_IOUT
registers.about: Over-current fault/warn bits.

registers.name: STATUS_INPUT
registers.about: Input (VIN) UV/OV + unit-off bits. Device-global.

registers.name: STATUS_TEMPERATURE
registers.about: Over-temp fault/warn bits.

registers.name: STATUS_CML
registers.about: Comms/memory/logic fault (bad command, bad data, flash fault).

registers.name: STATUS_MFR_SPECIFIC
registers.about: TI-specific rail status (GPI-driven faults, resequence errors).

registers.name: READ_VIN
registers.about: Measured input voltage (device-global).

registers.name: READ_VOUT
registers.about: Measured output voltage of the selected rail. Compare against VOUT_COMMAND and the UV/OV limits.

registers.name: READ_IOUT
registers.about: Measured rail current (if sensed).

registers.name: READ_TEMPERATURE_1
registers.about: Temperature (internal or external sensor).

registers.name: MFR_ID
registers.about: ASCII 'TI'. Read block (or 1 byte at a time on the shell).

registers.name: MFR_MODEL
registers.about: ASCII part model, e.g. 'UCD9090' / 'UCD90160'. PRIMARY part-per-address discriminator.

registers.name: MFR_REVISION
registers.about: Silicon/firmware revision.

registers.name: IC_DEVICE_ID
registers.about: Block read: TI device-id string identifying the exact UCD die. Secondary discriminator / live part confirm.

registers.name: IC_DEVICE_REV
registers.about: Device revision block.

registers.name: MFR_GPO_SELECT
registers.about: TI MFR-specific: select which GPO to configure. (FW ucd9090_enable_gpo writes 0xFA then 0xFB.)

registers.name: MFR_GPO_CONFIG
registers.about: TI MFR-specific: configure/drive the selected GPO. bit3 = GPO state readback (FW polls this). These GPOs gate downstream enables = part of the sequencing/dependency fabric.

mfr_sequencing_note: UCD9090/90160 store the full rail-sequencing + PGOOD/GPI dependency fabric (RAIL-to-RAIL 'sequence on/off dependencies', GPI fault responses, GPO logic, resequence timing) in device CONFIG, not in the standard PMBus command set. TI exposes them through MFR_SPECIFIC commands in the 0xD0..0xFF range (e.g. GPIO config 0xFA/0xFB above; the rest are documented register-by-register only in the TI 'UCDxxxx PMBus Command Reference' app notes, and are easiest to read/write with TI Fusion Digital Power GUI). The firmware here only ever drives OPERATION (0x01) + GPO (0xFA/0xFB) + PAGE (0x00) + reads voltages/status; it does NOT reprogram the dependency fabric at runtime - that config is burned at the factory into UCD flash via STORE_DEFAULT_ALL (0x11). So for sequencing analysis: TON_DELAY/TOFF_DELAY (0x60/0x64) per page give the time-ordered sequence directly, and the GPO/GPI dependency detail needs Fusion GUI + the TI command-ref app note (cited, not re-derived here). For boot-failure triage the per-page TON_DELAY ordering + STATUS_VOUT + READ_VOUT are sufficient and fully shell-readable.
